prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1056; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound in the left lane on a dry roadway in League City, Texas, when the vehicle drifted into the oncoming lane and collided head-on with the northbound vehicle operated by Driver 2. Both vehicles sustained front-end damage consistent with the reported impact, and the damage pattern is in line with the energy transfer expected from a low-speed head-on collision. Driver 1 stated that the left wrist struck the steering wheel and that pain and swelling followed immediately, a description that fits the force of the contact. Driver 2 and two independent witnesses gave accounts that match the sequence of events, and photographs taken at the scene support them. Responding officers and witnesses confirmed that Passenger was seated in the front right seat at the time of the collision. Minor older scratches were noted on the front bumper; these may predate this incident and were recorded for reference only. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
